arguments.claim: Mammography (MLO view) shows a well-circumscribed, oval, hyperdense mass in the right breast without calcifications or architectural distortion.
Ultrasound shows a well-circumscribed, oval, hypoechoic mass measuring approximately 29.7 x 14.0 mm with parallel orientation (wider than tall).
Ultrasound elastography of the mass shows mixed stiffness pattern (green and red areas) with a hardness index of 26%.
The mass demonstrates benign imaging features: well-circumscribed margins, oval shape, parallel orientation, and absence of suspicious calcifications or spiculation.

hypotheses.name: Fibroadenoma
hypotheses.rationale: Classic imaging features: well-circumscribed, oval, parallel-oriented mass on both mammography and ultrasound. Homogeneous hypoechoic appearance. Elastography shows mixed stiffness (26% hardness). Clinical presentation of mobile lump in 35F is classic.

hypotheses.name: Phyllodes tumor
hypotheses.rationale: Can appear similar to fibroadenoma but typically larger and more rapidly growing. Imaging features overlap significantly. Less likely given classic benign features.

hypotheses.name: Simple cyst
hypotheses.rationale: Unlikely as ultrasound shows solid hypoechoic mass, not anechoic with posterior enhancement.

hypotheses.name: Breast carcinoma
hypotheses.rationale: Very unlikely given well-circumscribed margins, oval shape, parallel orientation, and absence of suspicious features.

arguments.note: Imaging shows classic benign features: well-circumscribed, oval, parallel-oriented mass. Fibroadenoma is now the leading diagnosis.

differential_diagnoses.name: Phyllodes tumor
differential_diagnoses.why: Can appear similar to fibroadenoma on imaging with well-circumscribed margins and oval shape, but typically larger and more rapidly growing. Less likely given classic benign imaging features and lack of rapid growth history.

differential_diagnoses.name: Breast carcinoma
differential_diagnoses.why: Very unlikely given well-circumscribed margins, oval shape, parallel orientation, homogeneous appearance, and absence of suspicious features (spiculation, microcalcifications, posterior shadowing). Age 35 also makes malignancy less likely.

Mammography shows well-circumscribed, oval, hyperdense mass without calcifications or architectural distortion

uncertainty: Cannot definitively exclude phyllodes tumor without histology, as imaging features overlap with fibroadenoma

differential_diagnoses.name: Phyllodes tumor
differential_diagnoses.why: Phyllodes tumors can mimic fibroadenomas with well-circumscribed, oval masses. However, they are typically larger, grow more rapidly, and may show internal heterogeneity or cystic spaces. The classic benign features and stable appearance here make fibroadenoma more likely.

differential_diagnoses.name: Invasive ductal carcinoma
differential_diagnoses.why: Malignancy is unlikely given the well-circumscribed margins, oval shape, parallel orientation (wider than tall), and absence of spiculation, microcalcifications, or posterior acoustic shadowing. These features are strongly associated with benign pathology.

key_findings.fact: Mammography shows a well-circumscribed, oval, hyperdense mass in the right breast without calcifications or architectural distortion.
Ultrasound shows a well-circumscribed, oval, hypoechoic mass measuring approximately 29.7 x 14.0 mm with parallel orientation.
Ultrasound elastography shows a mixed stiffness pattern with a hardness index of 26%.
The mass demonstrates benign imaging features including well-circumscribed margins, oval shape, parallel orientation, and absence of suspicious calcifications or spiculation.

uncertainty: Histologic confirmation is required to definitively exclude phyllodes tumor, as imaging features can overlap.
